_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Based on the Tiny Block egg in https://github.com/pelican-eggs/games-standalone (MIT).
name: Tiny Block
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: A community world for Tiny Block, the 2D block sandbox game. Installs the chosen release of the headless server, checked against GitHub's checksum; it lists itself in the game's Online Worlds and needs no open port.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Tiny Block: downloads the chosen release of the headless server from its
# GitHub releases and checks it against GitHub's SHA-256. Worlds (in
# .local/share/godot) are never touched.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server

repo=hardtab/tinyblock-server
asset=tinyblock-server-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
[ "$(uname -m)" = x86_64 ] || fail "Tiny Block's server is only built for x86-64 (amd64) CPUs, and this node is $(uname -m)."

want="${VERSION:-latest}"
tag=$(gh-release tag "$repo" "$want" 2>/dev/null) ||
    fail "Tiny Block has no release $want. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as $(gh-release tag "$repo" latest 2>/dev/null || echo v0.2.32)."
sum=$(gh-release assets "$repo" "$tag" | awk -v a="$asset" '$1 == a { print $2 }')
[ -n "$sum" ] || fail "Tiny Block's release $tag has no Linux server."

if [ "$(cat .raptor-tinyblock 2>/dev/null)" = "$tag $sum" ] && [ -x tinyblock-server.x86_64 ]; then
    echo "Tiny Block $tag is already installed."
    exit 0
fi
build=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$build"; mkdir -p "$build/x"
trap 'rm -rf "$build"' EXIT
echo "Downloading Tiny Block $tag"
gh-release download "$repo" "$tag" "$asset" "$build/server.tar.gz" || fail "The download of Tiny Block failed. Reinstall to try again."
tar -xzf "$build/server.tar.gz" -C "$build/x" --strip-components=1
chmod +x "$build/x/tinyblock-server.x86_64"
cp -a "$build/x/." .
echo "$tag $sum" > .raptor-tinyblock
echo "Installed Tiny Block $tag."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The release to install, such as v0.2.32, or latest.

variables.name: World ID
variables.description: The world's save name. Keep it the same to keep the world across restarts.

variables.name: World name
variables.description: The name shown in the game's Online Worlds list.

variables.name: World mode
variables.description: How a new world is made: skyblock, floating_islands, procedural, one_block or challenge_run.

variables.name: Max players
variables.description: The most players that can be connected at once.
